title: Use These AI Video Prompts to Create Cinematic Videos From Text
excerpt: Want to turn your imagination into cinematic videos? These 10 copy-and-paste AI video prompts help you create realistic movie scenes, epic landscapes, futuristic cities, and professional-looking videos from simple text descriptions.
author: LokkeeVerse Editorial
content:
# How to Create Faceless YouTube Shorts Using AI for Free: A Beginner-Friendly Workflow

Creating faceless YouTube Shorts is a simple way to start a YouTube channel without showing your face or buying expensive equipment. With free AI tools, you can write scripts, generate voiceovers, find visuals, edit videos, and publish content directly from your computer or phone.

In this guide, you will learn how to create your first faceless YouTube Short using free tools, even if you have no video-editing experience.

## What Are Faceless YouTube Shorts?

Faceless YouTube Shorts are short vertical videos that do not require you to appear on camera. Instead, they use voiceovers, captions, images, animations, stock footage, or AI-generated visuals to tell a story.

Popular faceless content ideas include dark mysteries, celebrity stories, interesting facts, historical events, technology updates, motivational stories, and AI-related content.

The key is to choose a topic people want to watch and present it in an engaging way.

## Step 1: Choose a Niche for Your Channel

Before creating your first video, decide what kind of content you want to publish.

Here are some beginner-friendly niches to consider.

### Dark Mysteries and Unsolved Stories

Create short videos about unusual historical events, unexplained mysteries, strange discoveries, and interesting cases. These topics can encourage viewers to watch until the end when presented accurately and responsibly.

### Celebrity Stories and Pop Culture

Cover interesting celebrity facts, entertainment news, public controversies, and trending pop-culture stories. Always verify information using reliable sources, especially when discussing recent events.

### AI Tools and Technology

Show viewers useful AI websites, new technology, productivity tips, and creative ways to use AI tools.

### Interesting Facts

Create short videos about science, space, history, animals, psychology, and everyday things people may not know.

Choose one niche initially so viewers can understand what your channel offers.

## Step 2: Write Your Script With ChatGPT

You do not need to write every script from scratch. ChatGPT can help you brainstorm ideas, structure your story, and create a strong opening hook.

Visit ChatGPT at https://chatgpt.com/ and ask it to create a script for your chosen topic.

For example, you can use this prompt:

Create a 30-second YouTube Shorts script about a fascinating mystery. Start with a powerful hook that grabs attention within the first three seconds. Explain the story in simple, engaging language. Keep the pacing fast, use short sentences, and end with a memorable fact or question. Include suggested visuals for each scene. Do not invent facts, and clearly identify anything that is uncertain.

Review the script before using it. Check names, dates, statistics, and other factual claims, particularly if your video covers real people or events.

A good 30-second Short usually needs a concise script that can be spoken naturally without rushing.

## Step 3: Create a Voiceover for Free

Once your script is ready, turn it into narration.

You can use CapCut's text-to-speech feature or explore ElevenLabs at https://elevenlabs.io/. Both offer options for experimenting with AI-generated voices, although available free features and usage limits can change.

Choose a voice that suits your niche. A mystery video may benefit from a calm, suspenseful voice, while an entertainment video may work better with an energetic narration style.

Listen to the complete voiceover before moving to the next step. Correct awkward pronunciations, remove unnecessary pauses, and make sure the narration sounds natural.

You can also record your own voice if you prefer. A clear recording in a quiet room can work well without expensive equipment.

## Step 4: Find Visuals for Your Video

Your visuals should support the story rather than simply fill the screen.

You can find free stock footage on Pexels at https://www.pexels.com/videos/ and Pixabay at https://pixabay.com/videos/.

Search for footage that matches the scenes in your script. For example, a video about space could use images of planets, stars, and spacecraft, while a historical mystery might use relevant locations, old photographs, or atmospheric landscapes.

You can also use AI image generators to create original images or AI video tools to animate selected scenes. Free access and generation limits vary between services.

When choosing visuals, consider the following tips.

- Match each scene to the words being spoken.
- Use vertical footage where possible.
- Avoid using the same image for too long.
- Add movement through gentle zooms or transitions when appropriate.
- Check the licensing terms before using stock footage, music, or other assets.
- Avoid presenting fictional or AI-generated scenes as genuine evidence of real events.

## Step 5: Edit Your Short in CapCut

Visit https://www.capcut.com/ to start editing your video. You can also use the mobile app if that is more convenient.

Import your voiceover and the visuals you collected. Arrange the clips in the order of your script and trim them to match the narration.

Set your project to a vertical 9:16 format, which is suitable for YouTube Shorts.

Next, add captions so viewers can follow the story even when their sound is turned off. Use a readable font, strong contrast, and short lines of text. Make sure the captions match the spoken words.

You can also add background music and sound effects to improve the atmosphere. Keep them quieter than the narration so viewers can hear the story clearly.

Avoid excessive transitions, flashing effects, or unnecessary animations. Clean editing is often more effective than making every second visually complicated.

Before exporting, watch the entire video and check that the audio, captions, visuals, and pacing work together.

## Step 6: Create an Engaging Title

Your title should tell viewers what makes the video interesting without misleading them.

For example, a video about an unusual historical discovery could use a title such as “The Strange Discovery That Changed History.”

A video about AI could use “This Free AI Tool Can Turn Images Into Videos.”

Choose a title that accurately represents the content. Avoid promising shocking revelations or unbelievable results that the video does not deliver.

You can also write a short description explaining the video and include relevant hashtags where appropriate. A few relevant hashtags are generally more useful than a long list of unrelated ones.

## Step 7: Upload Your Video to YouTube

Open YouTube Studio at https://studio.youtube.com/ and upload your finished video.

Check the title, description, audience settings, and any other relevant publishing options. Follow YouTube's current requirements for Shorts and disclose realistic altered or synthetic content when the platform requires it.

After publishing, review how viewers respond to your content. Pay attention to how many people choose to watch, how long they stay, and which topics receive the strongest engagement.

Use these insights to improve your next video rather than judging your entire channel by the performance of one upload.

## A Simple Free Tool Setup

For your first few videos, you can keep your workflow simple.

Use ChatGPT to develop ideas and write scripts. Use CapCut for voiceovers, editing, captions, and sound adjustments. Use Pexels or Pixabay for suitable stock footage. Use YouTube Studio to publish videos and review performance.

You do not need to pay for several subscriptions before you begin. Start with the free features available to you and upgrade only when you understand what your channel actually needs.

## How Long Does It Take to Create One Short?

Your first video may take longer because you are learning the tools. As you become more comfortable, you can use a repeatable process.

Spend a few minutes choosing a topic and researching it. Write and check the script, generate the narration, collect the visuals, edit the video, and review the finished result before publishing.

The exact time depends on the complexity of your video and how much original footage or research it requires.

Do not sacrifice accuracy and quality simply to publish faster.

## Common Mistakes to Avoid

One mistake is publishing AI-generated content without checking it. AI tools can produce inaccurate information, so fact-check your scripts before uploading them.

Another mistake is copying other creators' videos. Reusing someone else's footage, scripts, or editing without the necessary rights or meaningful original contribution can create copyright and monetization problems.

You should also avoid producing large numbers of nearly identical videos with little original value. AI can make production easier, but your ideas, storytelling, research, and editing should give viewers a reason to watch your content.

Finally, do not assume that views automatically translate into income. YouTube monetization depends on eligibility requirements, current platform policies, and the nature of your content.

## Final Thoughts

Creating faceless YouTube Shorts with AI does not have to be expensive. You can start with ChatGPT for ideas and scripts, free footage from Pexels or Pixabay, CapCut for narration and editing, and YouTube Studio for publishing.

Begin with one niche, create a short video, and learn from the results. As your skills improve, experiment with stronger hooks, better storytelling, more relevant visuals, and clearer narration.

The goal is not simply to make videos quickly. It is to create original, useful, or entertaining content that gives people a reason to keep watching and return to your channel.
